Author: Ajay Bhanot
Bench: Ajay Bhanot

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:AHC:95113 Court No. - 45 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 19443 of 2025 Applicant :- Shavez Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Asheesh Kumar Tiwari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.
Learned A.G.A contends that no instructions have been forthcoming from the police authorities.
There is no cause for failing to provide instructions to the learned Government Advocate despite advance notice of the bail application.
The notice was served on 29.05.2025.
Liberty of citizens is too sacrosanct and cannot be held to ransom by callous attitude of the police authorities.
The bail application is being heard on merits.

By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in S.T. No.1791 of 2024, Case Crime No.152 of 2024 at Police Station-Budhana, District-Muzaffar Nagar under Shavez vs State Of U.P. on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110940494/
1 Sections 498A, 304B, 316 of the IPC and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act.
The applicant is in jail since 21.04.2024.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 06.12.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Asheesh Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned A.G.A.-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
2. The applicant did not torture the deceased nor demanded dowry.
3. The relationship between the applicant and his wife were harmonious.
Two children were born in the wedlock.
4. The deceased was a sensitive lady who became depressed as a result of differences with her family members.
The said family members pressurized and constantly insulted her which aggravated her mental condition.
5. On the fateful day, the deceased succumbed to depression and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide by hanging.
6. The postmortem report opines the cause of death as asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

7. Injuries depicted in the postmortem report consistent with hanging are:
(i) Nature of ligature mark.
(ii). No abnormality was detected in the hyoid bone 8.
The applicant did not aid or abet the suicide.
9. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
10. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of her influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.

In wake of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case,
the bail application is allowed.

Shavez vs State Of U.P. on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110940494/
2
Let the applicant-Shavez be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
